media.title: Grade 3 English Q1 Ep1: Picture Talk

items.prompt: Picture Talk: A picture shows a boy beside a yellow kite. Which sentence describes a visible detail?

options.text: A boy stands beside a yellow kite.
The boy will win a race.
The kite belongs to his sister.

items.explanation: The sentence names only details that can be seen in the picture.

items.prompt: Picture Talk: Which question helps you observe a picture carefully?

options.text: What colors and objects can I see?

items.explanation: Looking for colors and objects focuses on observable picture details.

items.prompt: Picture Talk: A picture shows a cat under a table. Which detail tells the cat’s position?

options.text: The cat is under the table.

items.explanation: “Under the table” tells where the cat is visible.

items.prompt: Picture Talk: Which sentence gives a useful detail about a picture of a market?

options.text: The baskets were bought last week.
The market will be crowded tomorrow.
Three red baskets sit near the door.

items.explanation: The sentence reports objects, color, and location that can be observed.

items.prompt: Picture Talk: When sharing what a picture shows, which response is strongest?

options.text: I see a small boat on the blue water.
I think the artist felt tired.

items.explanation: A strong picture description names visible details without guessing.

media.title: Grade 3 English Q1 Ep2: Noting Details

items.prompt: Noting Details: A note says, “Lena carried two blue bags to school.” Who carried the bags?
items.explanation: The sentence names Lena as the person carrying the bags.

items.prompt: Noting Details: “The puppy slept on the soft mat.” Which detail is stated?

options.text: The puppy slept on a soft mat.

items.explanation: The answer repeats the stated action, place, and describing word.

items.prompt: Noting Details: “A red bus stopped at 8 o’clock.” Which detail is NOT stated?
items.explanation: The sentence does not say whether the bus was full.

items.prompt: Noting Details: Which note records the most precise detail from “Mia found three shells on the beach”?

options.text: Mia found three shells on the beach.

items.explanation: The first note keeps the person, number, object, and place.

items.prompt: Noting Details: After reading a short passage, what should a detail note include?

options.text: A fact stated in the passage
A feeling unrelated to the text

items.explanation: A detail note should be supported directly by what the passage says.

media.title: Grade 3 English Q1 Ep3: Character and Ending

items.prompt: Character and Ending: “Sam shared his lunch when Jo forgot hers.” What character trait does Sam show?
items.explanation: Sharing food to help Jo shows kindness.

items.prompt: Character and Ending: “The story takes place beside a quiet river.” Which part of a story is named?
items.explanation: The setting tells where the story happens.

items.prompt: Character and Ending: A story problem is “The lost puppy cannot find home.” Which ending resolves it?

options.text: Mina follows its tag and brings it home.
The story starts with a new problem.

items.explanation: Finding the home resolves the lost-puppy problem.

items.prompt: Character and Ending: Which order makes sense for a story about planting a seed?

options.text: See a sprout, water it, plant the seed.
See a sprout, plant the seed, water it.
Water it, see a sprout, plant the seed.
Plant the seed, water it, see a sprout.

items.explanation: Planting comes before watering and the sprout appearing.

items.prompt: Character and Ending: “Nico practiced every day and finished the race.” What can readers infer about Nico?
items.explanation: Daily practice and finishing show determination.

media.title: Grade 3 English Q1 Ep4: Closer Look at Endings

items.prompt: Closer Look at Endings: “The storm stopped, and the family dried the wet blankets.” What does this ending show?
items.explanation: Drying the blankets shows the family responding to the storm.

items.prompt: Closer Look at Endings: “Kai lost his library book. He searched every room.” Which ending fits best?

options.text: Kai started a different story in the middle.
Kai found the book under his bed and returned it.
Kai forgot what a library was.

items.explanation: Finding and returning the book gives the problem a clear ending.

items.prompt: Closer Look at Endings: Which sentence could close a story about planting flowers?

options.text: Next, she dug a small hole.
First, Ana chose a packet of seeds.
Soon, bright flowers opened in the garden.

items.explanation: The flowers opening completes the planting sequence.

items.prompt: Closer Look at Endings: What should a satisfying story ending do?

options.text: Show what happens after the problem

items.explanation: An ending shows the result of the story’s main problem or events.

items.prompt: Closer Look at Endings: “The class cleaned the park. At last, the path was clear.” Which line is the ending?

options.text: At last, the path was clear.

items.explanation: “At last” signals the result that closes the action.

media.title: Grade 3 English Q1 Ep5: Lesson in a Diary

items.prompt: Lesson in a Diary: Which feature belongs in a simple diary entry?

options.text: A date and a personal account
A list of dictionary guide words

items.explanation: A diary records a personal experience, usually with a date.

items.prompt: Lesson in a Diary: “Tuesday, May 7 — I fed our new kitten. I felt proud.” What is the writer sharing?
items.explanation: The entry tells what happened and how the writer felt.

items.prompt: Lesson in a Diary: Which point of view fits a child writing about their own day?
items.explanation: “I” shows the writer is telling about their own experience.

items.prompt: Lesson in a Diary: Why does a diary entry often use a date?

options.text: To show when the event happened

items.explanation: The date places the personal event in time.

items.prompt: Lesson in a Diary: Which line sounds most like a diary reflection?

options.text: I felt calm after helping Dad.

items.explanation: A reflection tells the writer’s thought or feeling about an event.

media.title: Grade 3 English Q1 Ep 6 Writing Your Own Simple Diary

items.prompt: Writing Your Own Simple Diary: Which opening gives a diary entry a clear date?
items.explanation: A day and date tell when the diary event happened.

items.prompt: Writing Your Own Simple Diary: Which sentence uses first person for your own diary?

options.text: The children planted a bean seed.

items.explanation: The pronoun “I” shows the writer is describing their own experience.

items.prompt: Writing Your Own Simple Diary: Which detail makes “I visited the park” more specific?

options.text: I fed two ducks near the pond.

items.explanation: The detail names an action, number, animal, and place.

items.prompt: Writing Your Own Simple Diary: Which order is clearest for a diary about baking?

options.text: I wrote the ending before any event happened.
I tasted bread, then mixed batter, then baked it.
I baked it before gathering ingredients and mixing.
I mixed the batter, baked it, then tasted the bread.

items.explanation: The sequence follows the actions from preparation to result.

items.prompt: Writing Your Own Simple Diary: Which closing adds a personal reflection?

options.text: I was proud when the bread came out warm.
The kitchen is next to the hall.

items.explanation: The closing shares the writer’s feeling about the event.

media.title: Grade 3 English Q1 Ep7: Different Kinds of Sentences

items.prompt: Different Kinds of Sentences: Which sentence makes a statement?
items.explanation: A statement gives information and ends with a period.

items.prompt: Different Kinds of Sentences: Which sentence asks a question?
items.explanation: The question asks for information and ends with a question mark.

items.prompt: Different Kinds of Sentences: Which sentence gives a command?

options.text: Please line up by the door.

items.explanation: A command tells someone what to do.

items.prompt: Different Kinds of Sentences: Which sentence shows strong feeling?
items.explanation: The exclamation mark and excited wording show strong feeling.

items.prompt: Different Kinds of Sentences: Which punctuation matches “Did you finish your drawing__”?
items.explanation: A question ends with a question mark.

media.title: Grade 3 English Q1 Ep8: Sentence Galore

items.prompt: Sentence Galore: Which group of words is a complete sentence?
items.explanation: It has a subject, an action, and a complete thought.

items.prompt: Sentence Galore: Which choice completes “The children ___ in the yard”?
items.explanation: “Play” supplies the action needed for a complete sentence.

items.prompt: Sentence Galore: Which sentence begins with a capital letter and ends correctly?
items.explanation: A sentence begins with a capital and ends with a period.

items.prompt: Sentence Galore: Which choice is a fragment, not a complete sentence?
items.explanation: “After the rain” leaves the thought unfinished.

items.prompt: Sentence Galore: Which sentence combines the ideas clearly?

options.text: Lina drew a star, and Ben colored it.
Lina drew a star Ben colored.

items.explanation: The conjunction “and” joins the two complete ideas clearly.

media.title: Grade 3 English Q1 Ep 9 Identify and use common and proper nouns correctly

items.prompt: Common and Proper Nouns: Which word is a proper noun?
items.explanation: “Manila” is the specific name of a city.

items.prompt: Common and Proper Nouns: Which pair has a common noun followed by a proper noun?
items.explanation: “River” is general; “Pasig River” is a specific name.

items.prompt: Common and Proper Nouns: Which sentence capitalizes the proper noun correctly?
items.explanation: “Cebu” is a proper name and begins with a capital letter.

items.prompt: Common and Proper Nouns: In “Teacher Rosa reads,” which word is a common noun?
items.explanation: “Teacher” names a kind of person, not one unique person.

items.prompt: Common and Proper Nouns: Which label fits “school” in “Bayanihan School”?
items.explanation: “School” is common by itself, while the full school name is proper.

media.title: Grade 3 English Q1 Ep10: Into the World of Proper Nouns and Common Nouns

items.prompt: Proper Nouns and Common Nouns: Which word names one specific place?
items.explanation: “Davao” names one particular place.

items.prompt: Proper Nouns and Common Nouns: Which word is a common noun?
items.explanation: “Mountain” names a general kind of landform.

items.prompt: Proper Nouns and Common Nouns: Which sentence uses capitals for a person and a place?
items.explanation: “Carlo” and “Baguio” are specific names and need capitals.

items.prompt: Proper Nouns and Common Nouns: Which pair is two proper nouns?
items.explanation: “Maria” is a name and “Friday” is a named day.

items.prompt: Proper Nouns and Common Nouns: Which revision changes the common noun “river” into a proper name?
items.explanation: “Agusan River” gives the river a specific name.

media.title: Grade 3 English Q1 Ep11: Singular to Plural Form of Regular Nouns

items.prompt: Singular to Plural Regular Nouns: What is the plural of “book”?
items.explanation: Add -s to “book” to make “books.”

items.prompt: Singular to Plural Regular Nouns: What is the plural of “bus”?
items.explanation: Words ending in s usually add -es: bus becomes buses.

items.prompt: Singular to Plural Regular Nouns: What is the plural of “box”?
items.explanation: Words ending in x add -es: box becomes boxes.

items.prompt: Singular to Plural Regular Nouns: Which sentence uses a regular plural noun?

options.text: Three dish are on the table.
Three dish is on the table.
Three dishies are on the table.
Three dishes are on the table.

items.explanation: “Dishes” is the regular plural of “dish.”

items.prompt: Singular to Plural Regular Nouns: Which spelling correctly makes “baby” plural?
items.explanation: Change y to i and add -es: baby becomes babies.

media.title: Grade 3 English Q1 Ep 12: Plural Forms of Frequently Occurring Plural Nouns

items.prompt: Frequently Occurring Plural Nouns: What is the plural of “child”?
items.explanation: “Children” is the plural form of “child.”

items.prompt: Frequently Occurring Plural Nouns: What is the plural of “mouse”?
items.explanation: “Mice” is the irregular plural of “mouse.”

items.prompt: Frequently Occurring Plural Nouns: Which sentence uses “feet” correctly?
items.explanation: “Feet” is the plural of “foot,” and “are” matches the plural subject.

items.prompt: Frequently Occurring Plural Nouns: Which pair shows singular and irregular plural?
items.explanation: “Tooth” changes to “teeth,” not by simply adding -s or -es.

items.prompt: Frequently Occurring Plural Nouns: Choose the correct word: “Two ___ ran across the field.”
items.explanation: “Geese” is the plural form of “goose.”

media.title: Grade 4 English Q1 Ep1: Understanding a Paragraph

items.prompt: Understanding a Paragraph: In a paragraph about planting herbs, which sentence is the topic sentence?

options.text: Growing herbs at home is a useful activity.
First, fill a pot with soil.
Next, place the pot near sunlight.

items.explanation: The topic sentence introduces the paragraph’s main subject.

items.prompt: Understanding a Paragraph: Which detail supports “Reading every day builds skills”?

options.text: A child reads ten pages after dinner.

items.explanation: Reading ten pages directly supports the idea about building reading skills.

items.prompt: Understanding a Paragraph: What is the main idea of a paragraph whose details explain sorting trash into bins?

options.text: Sorting trash helps keep places clean.

items.explanation: The main idea summarizes the shared point of the details.

items.prompt: Understanding a Paragraph: Which sentence could conclude a paragraph about saving water?

options.text: The faucet is made of metal.
Small water-saving habits help protect our supply.

items.explanation: The conclusion restates the paragraph’s point about saving water.

items.prompt: Understanding a Paragraph: Which detail does NOT belong in a paragraph about caring for a pet?

options.text: I give the dog fresh water.
I take the dog for walks.

items.explanation: The kite detail is unrelated to caring for a pet.

media.title: Grade 4 English Q1 Ep2: Dictionary and it's Parts

items.prompt: Dictionary and Its Parts: In a dictionary, what do guide words at the top of a page show?

options.text: The first and last entries on the page

items.explanation: Guide words show the alphabet range of entries on that page.

items.prompt: Dictionary and Its Parts: In the entry “bright, adjective, giving off much light,” what is the definition?

options.text: the word at the top of the page

items.explanation: The definition explains what “bright” means.

items.prompt: Dictionary and Its Parts: Which part tells that “quickly” is an adverb?
items.explanation: A part-of-speech label identifies how a word works in a sentence.

items.prompt: Dictionary and Its Parts: Which word would come first in dictionary order?
items.explanation: “Ant” comes first because n comes before p, w, and pp in the comparison.

items.prompt: Dictionary and Its Parts: What does a pronunciation guide help a reader do?
items.explanation: A pronunciation guide shows how to say a word.

media.title: Grade 4 English Q1 Ep3: Parts of a Simple Paragraph

items.prompt: Parts of a Simple Paragraph: Which sentence is the topic sentence?

options.text: Our class garden needs daily care.

items.explanation: The topic sentence tells what the whole paragraph will explain.

items.prompt: Parts of a Simple Paragraph: Which sentence is a supporting detail for “Rainforests have many kinds of life”?

options.text: Rainforests are a kind of book.
Toucans, insects, and trees live there.

items.explanation: The examples of living things support the rainforest topic.

items.prompt: Parts of a Simple Paragraph: Which sentence is a concluding sentence?

options.text: Next, place it in the bin.
For these reasons, recycling is worth practicing.

items.explanation: “For these reasons” signals a closing thought.

items.prompt: Parts of a Simple Paragraph: Which order builds a clear paragraph?
items.explanation: A simple paragraph usually introduces, explains, then closes its idea.

items.prompt: Parts of a Simple Paragraph: Which sentence does NOT support a paragraph about bicycle safety?

options.text: Use lights when it is dark.

items.explanation: The fruit sentence does not relate to bicycle safety.

media.title: Grade 4 English Q1 Ep4: Dictionary, Thesaurus, and Online Resource

items.prompt: Dictionary, Thesaurus, and Online Resource: Which resource gives a word’s definition and pronunciation?
items.explanation: A dictionary provides meanings and pronunciation information.

items.prompt: Dictionary, Thesaurus, and Online Resource: Which resource helps you find a synonym for “tiny”?
items.explanation: A thesaurus lists words with similar meanings.

items.prompt: Dictionary, Thesaurus, and Online Resource: Which tool is best for checking a current bus schedule?
items.explanation: An online resource can provide current schedule information.

items.prompt: Dictionary, Thesaurus, and Online Resource: You need the meaning of “fragile.” Which search is most useful?
items.explanation: A definition search is designed to explain the word’s meaning.

items.prompt: Dictionary, Thesaurus, and Online Resource: What is a safe habit when using an online resource?

options.text: Use a trusted site and check with an adult.
Share your password with the site.

items.explanation: Trusted sources and adult guidance help make online research safer.

media.title: Grade 4 English Q1 Ep5: Identifying Various Text Types

items.prompt: Identifying Various Text Types: “First, crack two eggs. Then, stir the mixture.” What text type is this?
items.explanation: The steps and ingredients make this a recipe.

items.prompt: Identifying Various Text Types: “Dear Aunt May, Thank you for the book. Love, Pia.” What text type is this?
items.explanation: A greeting, message, and sign-off identify a personal letter.

items.prompt: Identifying Various Text Types: “The moon reflects light from the sun.” What text type best fits?
items.explanation: The sentence gives a fact, so it fits informational text.

items.prompt: Identifying Various Text Types: “Nina opened the gate and heard a bell.” What text type best fits?
items.explanation: The sentence tells an event with a character and action.

items.prompt: Identifying Various Text Types: Which clue helps identify a poem?

options.text: Lines arranged for rhythm or imagery

items.explanation: Poems often use lines, rhythm, or vivid imagery.

media.title: Grade 4 English Q1 Ep6: Noting Significant Details of Various Text Types

items.prompt: Noting Significant Details of Various Text Types: A news note says, “The school team won on Friday at the town gym.” Which place is named?
items.explanation: The note names the town gym as the place.

items.prompt: Noting Significant Details of Various Text Types: A recipe says, “Mix flour and water, then bake for 20 minutes.” How long is the baking time?
items.explanation: The recipe states a baking time of 20 minutes.

items.prompt: Noting Significant Details of Various Text Types: A letter begins, “Dear Ben.” Who is the letter addressed to?
items.explanation: The greeting names Ben as the recipient.

items.prompt: Noting Significant Details of Various Text Types: “The rabbit hid in the hollow log during the rain.” Where did it hide?
items.explanation: The sentence directly gives the rabbit’s hiding place.

items.prompt: Noting Significant Details of Various Text Types: Which note best captures a stated detail from an informational text about bees?

options.text: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower.
The page will be longer tomorrow.

items.explanation: The first note states a concrete fact about bees.

media.title: Grade 4 English Q1 Ep7: Identifying the Meanings of Unfamiliar Words Through Structural Analysis

items.prompt: Structural Analysis: In “unfair,” what does the prefix un- tell you?
items.explanation: The prefix un- often means “not” or the opposite.

items.prompt: Structural Analysis: In “hopeful,” what does the suffix -ful suggest?
items.explanation: The suffix -ful means “full of.”

items.prompt: Structural Analysis: Which word part is the base word in “replaying”?
items.explanation: “Play” is the base word; re- and -ing are added parts.

items.prompt: Structural Analysis: What does “careless” most likely mean?
items.explanation: The suffix -less means “without.”

items.prompt: Structural Analysis: Which word can be understood as “a person who teaches”?
items.explanation: The base teach plus -er names a person who teaches.

media.title: Grade 4 English Q1 Ep8: Identifying the Meanings of Unfamiliar Words Through Structural Analysis

items.prompt: Structural Analysis: In “rewrite,” what does re- mean?
items.explanation: The prefix re- means to do something again.

items.prompt: Structural Analysis: What does “fearless” mean?
items.explanation: The suffix -less means “without.”

items.prompt: Structural Analysis: Which base word is in “playful”?
items.explanation: “Play” is the base word in “playful.”

items.prompt: Structural Analysis: What does “joyful” most likely mean?
items.explanation: The suffix -ful means “full of.”

items.prompt: Structural Analysis: Which word part helps you infer that “unhelpful” means not helpful?
items.explanation: The prefix un- changes the meaning to the opposite.

media.title: Grade 4 English Q1 Ep9: Connotation and Denotation

items.prompt: Connotation and Denotation: Which meaning of “home” is denotative?
items.explanation: Denotation is the direct, literal meaning of a word.

items.prompt: Connotation and Denotation: Which word has a positive feeling in this pair?
items.explanation: “Slender” often suggests an attractive or graceful thinness.

items.prompt: Connotation and Denotation: Which word has a negative feeling in this pair?
items.explanation: “Stubborn” can suggest refusing to change in an unfavorable way.

items.prompt: Connotation and Denotation: The denotation of “childish” is related to a child. What connotation can it have?
items.explanation: “Childish” can carry the negative feeling of being immature.

items.prompt: Connotation and Denotation: Which sentence uses “cheap” with a negative connotation?

options.text: That cheap toy broke in one day.
The cheap toy cost one coin.
The store listed a cheap toy.
The cheap toy was on sale.

items.explanation: Here “cheap” suggests poor quality, not only a low price.

media.title: Grade 4 English Q1 Ep10: Getting the Meaning of Words through Word Association and Classification

items.prompt: Word Association and Classification: Which word is most closely associated with “rain”?
items.explanation: An umbrella is used when it rains.

items.prompt: Word Association and Classification: Which group belongs to the category “fruits”?
items.explanation: Mango, banana, and papaya are all fruits.

items.prompt: Word Association and Classification: Which word does NOT belong with “violin, drum, flute”?
items.explanation: A blanket is not a musical instrument.

items.prompt: Word Association and Classification: Which pair is connected by a school association?
items.explanation: A teacher and classroom are directly connected in school.

items.prompt: Word Association and Classification: Which word completes the category “tools: hammer, saw, ___”?
items.explanation: A wrench is another tool.

media.title: Grade 1 MTB Q1 Ep1: Pagsasabi ng Tungkol sa Sarili at Sariling Karanasan

items.prompt: Alin ang buong pahayag tungkol sa sariling karanasan?

options.text: Ako ay naglaro sa bakuran kahapon.

items.explanation: Buong pahayag ito tungkol sa sariling ginawa at naranasan.

items.prompt: Alin ang maaaring sabihin upang ipakilala ang sarili?
items.explanation: Malinaw na ipinakikilala ng “Ako si Lino” ang sarili.

items.prompt: Kapag may nagkukuwento ng karanasan, ano ang mabuting gawin?
items.explanation: Ang maingat na pakikinig ay paggalang sa nagbabahagi.

items.prompt: Alin ang maayos na pagkakasunod ng pagsasalaysay?
items.explanation: Ang panimula, gitna, at wakas ay malinaw na ayos ng salaysay.

items.prompt: Ano ang dapat isama sa pagsasabi ng sariling karanasan?

options.text: Ang tunay na ginawa o naranasan

items.explanation: Ang sariling ginawa o naranasan ang dapat ibahagi.

media.title: Grade 1 MTB Q1 Ep2: Paggamit sa Terminong Kaugnay sa Aklat

items.prompt: Ano ang tawag sa harapang bahagi ng aklat?
items.explanation: Ang pabalat ang harapang bahagi ng aklat.

items.prompt: Saan karaniwang makikita ang pamagat ng aklat?
items.explanation: Karaniwang nakasulat ang pamagat sa pabalat.

items.prompt: Ano ang tawag sa taong sumulat ng aklat?
items.explanation: Ang may-akda ang sumulat ng aklat.

items.prompt: Ano ang tawag sa bawat bahagi ng aklat na binabasa?
items.explanation: Ang pahina ang bahaging binabasa sa aklat.

items.prompt: Alin ang wastong paggamit ng salitang “aklat”?
items.explanation: Ang aklat ay binabasa, kaya tama ang unang pahayag.

media.title: Grade 1 MTB Q1 Ep3: Pagbasa ng mga Salita

items.prompt: Alin ang tamang pagbasa sa pantig na “ba-sa”?
items.explanation: Ang “ba-sa” ay binabasa bilang “basa”.

items.prompt: Alin ang salitang may dalawang pantig?
items.explanation: Ang ba-hay ay may dalawang pantig.

items.prompt: Alin ang wastong paghahati sa pantig ng “saging”?
items.explanation: Ang wastong paghahati ay sa-ging.

items.prompt: Alin ang salitang nagsisimula sa pantig na “ma”?
items.explanation: Nagsisimula sa “ma” ang salitang mata.

items.prompt: Alin ang wastong baybay ng salitang binabasa?
items.explanation: Wasto ang “paaralan” dahil apat na pantig ito—pa-a-ra-lan—na tama ang dami ng letra sa bawat pantig.

media.title: Grade 1 MTB Q1 Ep4: Pagtukoy sa mga Salitang Magkasingtunog

items.prompt: Alin ang salitang ka-tunog ng “bahay”?
items.explanation: Magkatunog ang hulihan ng bahay at sabay.

items.prompt: Alin ang salitang ka-tunog ng “gabi”?
items.explanation: Magkatunog ang hulihan ng gabi at tabi.

items.prompt: Alin ang pares na magkasingtunog?
items.explanation: Magkatunog ang hulihan ng mesa at tasa.

items.prompt: Ano ang dapat ihambing upang malaman kung magkasingtunog ang dalawang salita?
items.explanation: Ang hulihan ng salita ang karaniwang pinakikinggan.

items.prompt: Alin ang HINDI ka-tunog ng “bata”?
items.explanation: Hindi magkatunog ang hulihan ng bata at bote.

media.title: Grade 1 MTB-MLE Q1 Ep 5 Pagbibigay ng Ngalan at Umpisa Tunog ng Bagay o Larawan

items.prompt: Anong salita ang tumutukoy sa gamit na sinusulatan?
items.explanation: Ang lapis ay gamit sa pagsulat.

items.prompt: Ano ang unang tunog ng salitang “mesa”?
items.explanation: Nagsisimula sa tunog /m/ ang mesa.

items.prompt: Alin ang nagsisimula sa tunog /b/?
items.explanation: Nagsisimula sa /b/ ang bola.

items.prompt: Alin ang ngalan ng bagay na ginagamit sa pag-inom?
items.explanation: Ang baso ay bagay na ginagamit sa pag-inom.

items.prompt: Ano ang unang tunog ng salitang “tasa”?
items.explanation: Nagsisimula sa tunog /t/ ang tasa.

media.title: Grade 1 MTB-MLE Q1 Ep 6 Pagpapahayag ng Ideya sa Pamamagitan ng Iba't ibang Simbolo

items.prompt: Ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng simbolong tsek (✓)?
items.explanation: Karaniwang tanda ng tama o napili ang tsek.

items.prompt: Ano ang maaaring ipahiwatig ng simbolong puso (♥)?
items.explanation: Ang puso ay karaniwang simbolo ng pagmamahal.

items.prompt: Ano ang ipinakikita ng palaso (→)?
items.explanation: Ang palaso ay nagpapakita ng direksiyon.

items.prompt: Kung may bilog na may pahilis na guhit, ano ang karaniwang ibig sabihin?
items.explanation: Ang bilog na may pahilis na guhit ay karaniwang tanda ng bawal.

items.prompt: Bakit ginagamit ang simbolo sa pagpapahayag?

options.text: Upang itago ang lahat ng ideya
Upang maipakita ang ideya sa maikling paraan

items.explanation: Nakakatulong ang simbolo na maipakita ang ideya nang maikli.

media.title: Grade 1 MTB Q1 Ep7: Paghubog sa Kahusayan sa Pagsagot sa mga Tanong Hango sa Kwentong Maririning ...

items.prompt: Habang nakikinig sa kuwentong maririnig, ano ang dapat tandaan?
items.explanation: Mahalagang tandaan ang tauhan at pangyayari sa kuwento.

items.prompt: Paano malalaman ang unang pangyayari sa kuwentong narinig?
items.explanation: Sa simula malalaman ang unang pangyayari.

items.prompt: Ano ang dapat gamitin sa pagsagot sa tanong tungkol sa narinig na kuwento?
items.explanation: Ang sagot ay dapat ibatay sa pahiwatig ng kuwento.

items.explanation: Sublimation skips the liquid state.

items.prompt: In sublimation, what happens to the solid?
items.explanation: In sublimation, a solid becomes gas.

items.prompt: Which sequence describes sublimation?
items.explanation: The sequence for sublimation is solid to gas.

items.prompt: How is sublimation different from melting?

options.text: It changes solid directly to gas.

media.title: Grade 4 Science Q1 Ep1: Ability of Material to Absorb Water

items.prompt: What does absorption mean for a material?
items.explanation: An absorbent material takes in water.

items.prompt: Which material commonly absorbs water well?
items.explanation: A sponge can absorb water.

items.prompt: Which material usually does not absorb water?
items.explanation: Plastic usually does not absorb water.

items.prompt: What observation can show absorption?

options.text: The material becomes wet as water enters it.
The material keeps water only above it.

items.explanation: Water entering a material shows absorption.

items.prompt: How can you compare absorbency fairly?

options.text: Give materials equal water and observe how much they take in.
Use a different amount for each.

items.explanation: Equal amounts make an absorbency comparison fair.

media.title: Grade 4 Science Q1 Ep2: Special Properties of Matter - Float or Sink in Water and Undergo Decay

items.prompt: When an object floats in water, where is it found?
items.explanation: A floating object stays at or near the water’s surface.

items.prompt: When an object sinks in water, where does it go?
items.explanation: A sinking object moves to the bottom.

items.prompt: What does decay do to dead material?

options.text: It breaks the material down over time.
It makes the material float forever.
It turns all material into metal.

items.explanation: Decay breaks down dead material over time.

items.prompt: Which observation tests whether an object floats or sinks?

options.text: Place it in water and observe its position.

items.explanation: Water placement reveals whether an object floats or sinks.

items.prompt: What is one environmental result of decay?

options.text: Materials break down and can return nutrients to soil.

items.explanation: Decay breaks materials down and can return nutrients to soil.

items.prompt: Before it is bent, what state is the material in this lesson?
items.explanation: Bending in this lesson acts on a solid material.

items.prompt: What can bending do to a solid?
items.explanation: Bending can change a solid’s shape.

items.prompt: What remains when one solid is bent?

options.text: the same material in a changed shape

items.explanation: Bending changes shape but can leave the same material.

items.prompt: Which property helps a solid bend without breaking?
items.explanation: Flexibility helps a material bend.

items.prompt: Which observation shows bending?

options.text: A straight solid curves after a force is applied.

items.explanation: A solid curving under force shows bending.

media.title: Grade 4 Science Q1 Ep4: Changes in Solid Materials when they are Pressed

items.prompt: Before it is pressed, what state is the material in this lesson?
items.explanation: Pressing in this lesson acts on a solid material.

items.prompt: What can pressing do to a solid?
items.explanation: Pressing can change a solid’s shape.

items.prompt: What happens to clay when it is pressed?

items.explanation: Pressing can make clay flatter or wider.

items.prompt: After pressing one solid, what may remain?

options.text: the same material in a new shape

items.prompt: Which observation shows pressing?

options.text: A solid flattens when force pushes on it.

items.explanation: Flattening under force shows pressing.

media.title: Grade 4 Science Q1 Ep5: Changes in Solid Materials when they are Hammered

items.prompt: What state is changed by hammering in this lesson?
items.explanation: Hammering acts on a solid material.

items.prompt: What can hammering do to a solid?

options.text: make it a liquid every time

items.explanation: Hammering can change a solid’s shape.

options.text: the same material with a changed shape

options.text: A solid changes shape after repeated blows.

media.title: Grade 4 Science Q1 Ep6: Describe the Changes that Solid Materials Undergo once they are Cut

items.prompt: What state of material is cut in this lesson?
items.explanation: Cutting in this lesson acts on a solid material.

items.prompt: What can cutting do to a solid?
items.explanation: Cutting can separate a solid into pieces.

items.prompt: After a solid is cut, what changes?

options.text: its state to gas every time

items.explanation: Cutting changes a solid’s size or shape.

items.prompt: What can remain the same after cutting?
items.explanation: Cutting can leave the same material in pieces.

items.prompt: Which observation shows cutting?
items.explanation: A solid becoming pieces shows cutting.

media.title: Grade 4 Science Q1 Ep8: Change in Materials when Mixed with Other Materials

items.prompt: What is formed when materials are mixed?
items.explanation: Mixing two or more materials forms a mixture.

items.prompt: Which example is a mixture?
items.explanation: Rice and beans together make a mixture because two different materials are combined.

items.prompt: Which choice is not a mixture?
items.explanation: One piece of wood is one material, not a mixture.

items.prompt: What should you do to study a mixture change?

options.text: Observe the materials before and after mixing.

items.explanation: Comparing before and after reveals changes from mixing.

items.prompt: What does mixing combine?
items.explanation: Mixing combines two or more materials, so the result is a mixture rather than one pure material.

media.title: Grade 4 Science Q1 Ep9: Changes in Materials when Mixed with Other Materials: Heterogenous Mixtures

items.prompt: What makes a mixture heterogeneous?

options.text: Different parts can be seen or are not uniform.

items.explanation: A heterogeneous mixture is not uniform throughout.

items.prompt: Which is a heterogeneous mixture?
items.explanation: A salad has different visible parts.

items.prompt: How can some heterogeneous mixtures be separated?

options.text: by sorting or picking out different parts
by changing all parts to gas

items.explanation: Visible parts can sometimes be separated by sorting.

items.prompt: What is true of the parts of a heterogeneous mixture?
items.explanation: In a heterogeneous mixture the parts stay separate enough to be told apart, because they are not blended evenly.

items.prompt: Which mixture is more uniform than heterogeneous?
items.explanation: Salt dissolved evenly in water looks the same throughout, so it is more uniform than a heterogeneous mixture.

media.title: Grade 4 Science Q1 Ep10: Changes in Materials when Mixed with Other Materials

items.prompt: What happens when two materials are mixed?

options.text: They are combined in one mixture.

items.prompt: Which combination is a mixture?
items.explanation: Water and sand together form a mixture because two different materials are combined.

items.prompt: Which action shows mixing?
items.explanation: Stirring two materials together is mixing, since it combines more than one material.

items.prompt: Why observe materials before and after mixing?

options.text: to notice changes and compare the materials

items.explanation: Before-and-after observations show what mixing changes.

items.prompt: Which statement about a mixture is correct?

options.text: It contains two or more materials.

items.explanation: A mixture contains two or more materials.

media.title: Grade 4 Science Q1 Ep13: Changes in Materials that are Useful and Harmful in the Environment

items.prompt: Which change is useful for reducing waste?
items.explanation: Reusing a clean container is useful because it means less waste is thrown away into the environment.

items.prompt: Which change can harm the environment?
items.explanation: Waste left on the ground can harm the environment.

items.prompt: What is a useful result of reusing a material?
items.explanation: Reusing materials can reduce the amount of waste.

items.prompt: Where can harmful waste cause problems?
items.explanation: Harmful waste can pollute soil or water.

items.prompt: Why study useful and harmful material changes?

options.text: To protect the environment and make responsible choices.
